style.outline: characters and props: dark brown-black outline about 3 px at 576 wide (5 px at 1080); coastline a thin dark line (2 px at 1080) with a pale soft halo on the sea side; land borders shown only by the change of fill colour; highlighted regions have a soft darker rim
style.shading: flat fills; flag-balls get a faint darker bottom-right and a soft contact shadow; no gradients on the map except the coast halo
style.shape_language: perfect circles for characters, wobbly noodle limbs with mitten hands, wooden plank signs on a post, real country shapes, small round icons (helmets, flags, houses)
style.texture: a crumpled-paper / hillshade mottling over land and sea, low contrast (about +-4% lightness), fixed to the map
style.type_ui: titles: hand-lettered rounded capitals in off-white with a dark outline and drop shadow, slightly rotated, in the top third; map labels: small letter-spaced serif capitals in dark brown; sign words: hand-lettered dark ink on wood; captions: short bold white phrases with a dark shadow near the bottom, numbers and key words amber, a character's line prefixed with a dash in its flag colour
style.motion_style: limited cut-out animation: balls bob, squash and blink, arms swing like puppets (held on twos), props and titles pop in with overshoot; mostly static framing per shot with slow push-ins; hard cuts between map locations; flashbacks washed out; travel shown by dotted routes and dashed arrows; one dark cinematic cutaway for the climax
style.signature: a plank sign planted in the disputed land whose single word changes through the story; flag-balls arguing on a real map; power shown by ball size
style.do_not_copy: the topic and every name in it (the colony, the empire, the neighbour, the ally, the alliance, the leader and the commander), all dates and numbers, the words on the signs and titles, the real archival photos in the portrait medallions, the 3D night scene; no watermark or handle is visible

story.summary: A countryball history short: a small empire refuses to give up a colony on a much bigger neighbour's coast, told as an argument between flag-balls on a real map, with a sign whose one word keeps changing until the last swap is the ending.
story.hook: 0-6 s: the whole conflict in one still image (a small flag-ball gripping a sign planted on a strip of the big ball's coast), the line "X insisted this strip of Y's coast was actually X", then a title with the place name and a year.
highlights: 0 s, 17-22 s, 46 s, 110 s: the sign motif: the word on the plank changes (name, colony, province, overseas province, finally the neighbour's name), so a political story becomes a fight over one word and the last swap is the payoff
9-15 s and 37-46 s: diplomacy as dialogue between flag-balls (character voices, dash captions), so each refusal lands as a joke
50-54 s: power shown as size: the neighbour ball swells to about 3x while the holder shrinks, under a title with the real ratio
88-101 s: tonal shift: the surrender is a dark, slow, almost silent cinematic scene, then an iris wipe back to the bright map for the aftermath
